h: Two girls in a violent, poor Naples neighborhood are bound by love and rivalry; an unsentimental portrait of a friendship that shapes both lives.

like.r: Another coming-of-age story built on bonds between girls, far gentler and more cheerful than Ferrante's harsh Naples.
A different slice of Italian history, told from the top of society, with the same sense of a world shifting under its people.
Sisterly loyalty and ambition among women who want more than their world allows, in a warmer key.

h: Two Irish teenagers keep drifting apart and back together across school and university; spare, aching, and mostly about what they fail to say.

like.r: Also follows two people who orbit each other over years, but with more jokes and a warmer, more conventional shape.
A love story made almost entirely of conversation and near-misses between two clever young people.
Also turns on a misunderstanding between lovers across class lines, with grander historical stakes.

h: A guarded Dublin student and her ex-girlfriend get tangled with an older married couple; clipped, intelligent, and emotionally evasive.

like.r: The author's warmer, more accessible novel, with the same cool prose and a tighter focus on one couple.
Another young woman's bruising education in love and class, set in a New York restaurant instead of Dublin.
Articulate people hurting one another in precise, talky scenes.

h: Two friends trade long emails about love, fame and civilization's decline while their own romances stumble along.

like.r: The easier entry into Rooney, with less essayistic musing and a more urgent central romance.
Another novel that holds private longing and big thoughts about the world in the same quiet frame.
Two lonely, articulate people drift toward connection while wondering what it all adds up to.

h: Two grieving brothers, a chess player and a barrister, fumble through new relationships after their father's death; looser and warmer than early Rooney.

like.r: The tighter, younger version of Rooney's concerns, centered on one couple rather than two brothers.
Another story of siblings shaped by loss and a parent's absence, told with great warmth.
A quiet, painful study of grief and family obligation that avoids easy consolation.

h: A Russian aristocrat is sentenced to house arrest in a grand Moscow hotel for decades and builds a rich life within its walls; urbane and gently funny.

like.r: Another courtly, formal protagonist who finds meaning inside a great house, though far more restrained and sad.
The same love of a grand hotel, impeccable manners and a vanished Europe, played as farce.
The same Russian upheaval seen from the other side, in a far more tragic and sprawling register.

h: A secretary on the rise in 1938 Manhattan is carried through its cocktail bars and society parties after a single chance meeting; glossy, wry, wistful.

like.r: The same glittering, class-conscious New York, narrated by an observer who sees its cost.
A clever young woman reinventing herself in Manhattan, with similar chic and underlying loneliness.
The author's more expansive and more comic novel, with the same polished prose and period charm.

t: All the Light We Cannot See
h: A blind French girl and a German radio prodigy move toward each other through the Second World War in very short, jewel-cut chapters.

like.r: Another Second World War story of children and the ways stories and sound keep them alive.
Occupied France seen through women's eyes, more melodramatic and less lyrical.
Another story about preserving wonder and tenderness in the middle of wartime horror.

h: Four college friends age in New York while one carries unspeakable damage; devastating, immersive, and very hard to read.

like.r: Another long, immersive novel about a damaged man shaped by early catastrophe, less relentless in its suffering.
A comparably harrowing story of love that cannot heal harm, set in working-class Glasgow.
Another tale of devoted male friendships under extreme loss, in 1980s Chicago.

h: The escape route becomes a literal train line, and each stop shows a different nightmare version of American racism.

like.r: The great novel of slavery's aftermath, more mythic and lyrical and even more demanding.
Follows slavery's reach across generations, in a more episodic and accessible form.
A grounded, unflinching depiction of the system Whitehead reimagines.

h: A bright Black teenager is sent to a brutal Florida reform school, where two friends hold different views on how to survive.

like.r: A classic of Black American life as a gauntlet, far more surreal and verbose.
Southern racial violence and its legacy, with ghosts and richer, more lyrical language.
Friendship as survival inside a cruel institution, though the tone is far more forgiving.

h: Abraham Lincoln mourns his young son in a cemetery crowded with chattering ghosts; a polyphonic, strange, unexpectedly moving book.

like.r: Another graveyard full of voices speaking from the afterlife, in poems rather than a novel.

like.t: A Visit from the Goon Squad
like.r: Another formally restless novel that uses many voices to approach time and loss.
Also uses the dead as a vantage point on what life was worth.

h: Two childhood friends start designing video games together and spend thirty years loving, resenting and needing each other.

like.t: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay
like.r: Another partnership of two creators building a medium and a bond across decades.
Shares the video-game love, but as a breezy adventure rather than a tender friendship drama.
Another story about brilliant friends who build something big and break their relationship doing it.

t: The Storied Life of A. J. Fikry
h: A grumpy widowed bookseller on a small island has his life rearranged by an abandoned child; sweet, bookish, and openly sentimental.

like.r: Another curmudgeon softened by unexpected company, with more grief and a bigger laugh.
A shorter, true bookshop love letter built from correspondence.
A cozy, bookish romance where the shop itself is a character.

h: After a flu wipes out civilization, a traveling Shakespeare troupe crosses the ruins; an elegy for what we made and what we keep.

like.r: A far bleaker and barer collapse story, with none of Mandel's faith in art and community.
Another braided, many-voiced novel that links distant lives across time.
A collapsing world and the stubborn hope left in it, in a more urgent and violent register.

h: A Ponzi scheme and its ruined victims, a remote Canadian hotel and a ghostly sense of other lives; elegant, moody and fragmented.

like.r: The author's best-loved book, with a comparable web of linked lives and a more hopeful center.
Another novel about wealth built on illusion and the people it leaves behind.
Another look at a financial collapse from the inside, focused on moral numbness.

t: My Year of Rest and Relaxation
h: A rich, beautiful young woman decides to sleep for a year with the help of prescription drugs; caustic, funny and quietly desperate.

like.r: The classic of a young woman's withdrawal from a world that wants her to perform.
The same author's earlier acid portrait of a self-loathing young woman, shaded darker and more noir.
Satirical dissection of Manhattan wealth and emptiness, with a much more violent narrator.

h: A Vietnamese American son writes a letter to his mother, who cannot read it, about war, labor, desire and love; poetic and bruising.

like.r: Another queer coming-of-age told with raw honesty and lyrical force.
Another Vietnamese diaspora narrative, here a spy satire and far more plot-driven.
A tender, wordless-leaning portrait of a queer youth growing up in poverty and silence.

h: A foster kid with a sharp mouth grows up in Appalachia through poverty, opioids and neglect; angry, funny and big-hearted.

like.r: The Victorian original this updates, with the same orphan's resilience and social outrage.
A memoir of the same region and addiction crisis, from a very different perspective.
Another tough young Appalachian survivor in a rough, poor and loyal community.

h: Shakespeare's wife and their son's death in plague-struck Stratford; a lush, wrenching novel about grief that never names its famous husband.

like.r: Another tactile Tudor-era novel, more political and armored, less about the heart.
A comparable story of grief tied to a child, set on an isolated shore.
The same period and playwright, played as sparkling comedy instead of lament.

h: The witch of Aiaia tells her own long life, from her cold divine family to exile on an island and her encounters with famous heroes.

like.r: Another Odyssey retold from a woman's side, shorter and sharper.
The Iliad seen from the women taken as spoils, grimmer and more realistic.
Another woman raised among gods who learns what humans are, in a blockbuster key.

h: The Iliad as a love story between Achilles and Patroclus; lush, heartbreaking, and aware of exactly where the myth is headed.

like.r: The same Trojan War seen from the captive women, grimmer and more realist, with Achilles as a menace.
The author's other myth retelling, centered on a witch instead of a warrior.
The same war on screen, with a loud and swordy approach and few of Miller's emotions.

h: A rule-obsessed, recently widowed grump keeps being interrupted by his loud new neighbors when he tries to end his life; funny and moving.

like.r: Another prickly loner slowly opened up by a warm, odd friendship.

like.t: The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry
like.r: A gentle, sad novel about an older man whose small gestures change his life.
Another grumpy widower and an unexpected young companion, with the same tears-and-laughter mix.

h: A failed bank robber takes a roomful of apartment-viewers hostage; a comic, warm novel in which the strangers' sorrows spill out.

like.r: The author's best-known novel, with the same blend of grief and farce around one lonely man.
Another comic ensemble that gradually reveals the depression under funny surfaces.
A hostage standoff gone sideways, with the same sympathy for a clumsy would-be criminal.

h: A mixed-race family in 1970s Ohio unravels after their favorite daughter turns up dead; a quiet, sorrowful portrait of what families fail to say.

like.r: Another family reshaped by a daughter's death, with a more overtly emotional and otherworldly approach.
Ng's next novel, with a more plotted suburban conflict and similar emotional weight.
A suburban family wrecked by a child's death and unable to talk about it.

h: A drifting artist and her daughter rent from a perfect Ohio family, and a custody fight spreads through the whole planned suburb.

like.r: Another suburb of polished surfaces and buried secrets, with more humor and a murder at the center.
Ng's quieter debut, with a family dissolving after a loss.
A suburban facade cracking open under repressed desire and ruinous secrets.

h: Twin sisters flee the same Southern town; one returns, the other passes as white; their daughters' lives circle their secrets.

like.r: The classic short novel of racial passing, tighter and more claustrophobic than Bennett's generational spread.
Another multigenerational saga of how race and history shape descendants.
A melodrama about a light-skinned daughter rejecting her mother's world, with similar stakes.

h: A brilliant chemist, shut out of 1960s science, becomes the host of a cooking show and quietly turns it into a classroom.

like.r: Another brilliant, prickly woman and her daughter, told with comic, caper-like energy.
Another mid-century story of women pushing against a rigged system, gentler and more sentimental.
Talented women in 1960s science fighting condescension with competence, and a crowd-pleasing finish.

h: An abandoned girl raised by the North Carolina marsh becomes the suspect in a local man's death; part nature poem, part love story, part trial.

like.r: Another long, nature-rich Southern novel about solitude and survival.
A Southern courtroom story with a child's perspective and an outsider on trial.
Another wild, self-reliant girl in a Southern wetland, told in impressionistic fashion.

t: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
h: A reclusive Hollywood legend finally tells a young journalist the story of her seven marriages; glossy, addictive and surprisingly sad.

like.r: The same author's rock-band equivalent, in oral-history form.
A narrator draws us into the glamour and loneliness of a self-invented icon.
Another faded star and an outsider drawn into her secrets, but in a much colder, sharper noir.

h: A 1970s rock band's rise and implosion told as an oral history, with a singer and songwriter whose chemistry wrecks everything.

like.t: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
like.r: Same author, similar nostalgic glamour and secrets, centered on a film star.
The 1970s rock scene from a nearby vantage, with a friendlier and funnier tone.
A memoir of the same era's music scene and a creative partnership, more poetic and true.

h: Three mothers at a school's trivia night and a death no one fully saw; gossip, comedy and domestic violence woven together.

like.r: Another smoothly told suburban drama in which motherhood hides darker lives.
A darker, nastier take on appearances in modern marriages.
A suburban marriage dissected as the polished surfaces crack, much bleaker and with no comic relief.

h: Between life and death, a depressed woman gets to try the lives she didn't live; earnest, easy and consoling.

like.r: An older story where a visit to other versions of a life changes a despairing person.
A despairing man shown what his life was worth, with a similar redemptive warmth.
Plays with the same idea of many lives, but with more literary density and history.

h: A solar-powered robot companion observes a sick girl's family with devotion and innocence; gentle, strange and quietly devastating.

like.r: The author's other novel of tender, doomed beings who accept their fate.
Another story of a made child-like machine longing to be loved.
A softer, more romantic look at emotional bonds with artificial beings.

h: An elderly couple walk through a post-Arthurian Britain beneath a mist of forgetting, searching for their son.

like.r: Ishiguro's masterwork of memory and regret, with a more realistic setting.
Another bleak, spare journey through a ruined land, focused on a pair who love each other.
A medieval pilgrimage haunted by large questions, in a more starkly philosophical form.

h: A boy survives a museum bombing and leaves with a stolen painting that shadows his drifting, guilty life for years.

like.r: Tartt's debut, shorter and more tightly plotted, about a group of elite students and a crime.
The orphan-with-a-secret-benefactor structure that Tartt openly echoes.
Another story of a drifting young man and a fatal, aestheticized lie.

h: A charismatic 18th-century false messiah gathers followers across Central Europe in this sprawling, encyclopedic, strange book.

like.r: Another learned, immersive historical novel about faith, heresy and knowledge.
A similarly rich, sprawling immersion in an earlier Europe.
A meditation on belief and doubt under pressure, in a very different time and place.

h: Linked voices from the 1980 Gwangju uprising, from a dead boy to those who survived him; brutal, tender and hard to shake.

like.r: Another book that makes the dead and the survivors share the page after state violence.
Also a Korean history seen through ordinary people, more traditional and sweeping.
A film treatment of the same Gwangju events, built on a more accessible human drama.

h: A coal merchant in 1985 Ireland finds something in a convent shed and must choose whether to act; short, restrained and powerful.

like.r: Another quiet, precise Irish novel of ordinary people and the church's long shadow.
A harsher dramatization of the Irish institutions behind Keegan's quiet tale.
Another short, restrained book about a man deciding what he is willing to see.

h: Huckleberry Finn retold from Jim's point of view, as a sharp, dryly funny and increasingly harrowing run for freedom.

like.r: The original, which Everett answers with a fully human and defiantly intelligent Jim.
Another reimagining of the escape from slavery, more allegorical and bleak.
A very different, violent revenge fantasy on slavery with its own dark humor.

h: A woman in a long hospital stay is visited by her estranged mother, and the two talk in half-sentences about everything but what hurts.

like.r: Strout's linked stories around a prickly teacher, broader, funnier and harder-edged.
Another quiet, intimate first-person voice reckoning with love across a family.
A slow accumulation of ordinary family moments that adds up to something big.

h: One kiss at a christening merges two families, and the children spend decades coping with what came after.

like.r: Patchett's more focused sibling story, with a similarly warm voice.
Another episodic, sharply observed look at family wounds.
A decades-spanning family drama that turns from funny to devastating.

h: A brother and sister are cast out of their glamorous childhood mansion and spend their lives drawn back to its windows.

like.r: Another of Patchett's multi-decade family novels, more scattered across time and households.
Another novel narrated by someone obsessed with a house and the life it represents.
A family of damaged siblings and a lost home, played as deadpan comedy.

h: A Seattle teenager pieces together emails and memos to find her brilliant, agoraphobic architect mother after she vanishes.

like.r: Another funny, off-kilter woman whose quirks hide real pain.
A similar comic ensemble that turns tender when sorrow slips in.
A similarly quick-witted voice in a story about family under strain, told with bounce.

h: A lighthouse keeper and his wife keep a baby that washes ashore; a quiet moral tragedy with real emotional force.

like.r: Another novel where a single decision unfolds into long consequences.
Another family drama built on a moral dilemma with no clean answer.
Another remote, windswept coastal setting with a marriage under strain.

h: A socially stranded Glasgow office worker with vodka weekends and a formal voice starts to open up to a kind colleague.

like.r: Another isolated, rigid protagonist slowly softened by unwanted companions.
A lighter, more romantic novel about a literal-minded narrator learning connection.
A lonely, eccentric woman and a patient road toward other people, more whimsical.

h: A young couple escapes a collapsing city through magical doors that open onto other countries; slim, fabulist and humane.

like.r: A more conventional and emotional exile story, with the same themes of loss and migration.
Another novel that blends realistic detail with speculative devices to look at human connection.
A quiet family story about displacement and belonging.

t: A Visit from the Goon Squad
h: Linked chapters jump across decades of a record producer and his assistant's circle, including one told in PowerPoint slides.

like.r: Another novel of nested, differently styled sections whose characters echo across time.
Another formally adventurous book that treats time and death with comedy and sadness.
Interlocking stories told out of order, for a very different kind of cool.

h: Nine people are drawn to trees and eventually to the barricades; a monumental ecological novel that makes forests feel like characters.

like.r: Another sprawling, generation-crossing novel about humans and forests.
The nonfiction version of the idea that trees communicate and cooperate.
A mythic story of forest versus industry, with the same reverence for living things.

h: Four generations of a Korean family in Japan endure prejudice, poverty and hard bargains; an old-fashioned saga with big feeling.

like.r: Another multigenerational family saga about belonging and prejudice, with episodes in two continents.
A comparable story of resilient women across historic upheaval.
A smaller, gentler immigrant family story from the same diasporic Korean experience.

h: Two half-sisters in 18th-century Ghana go separate ways, and each chapter follows one descendant through slavery's long reach.

like.r: The classic American saga of a family traced back to Africa, more linear and plain.
A denser, more mythic and shattering look at slavery's aftermath.
A historical drama of the slave trade told through a single dramatic case.

h: A Nigerian woman leaves for America, learns what being Black means there, and goes home to a love left unfinished.

like.r: Another funny, wide-ranging look at immigrant families and identity in London.
A chorus of Black British women with a similar blend of wit and anger.
Another emigrant woman torn between home and a new country, in a gentler key.

h: Thomas Cromwell quietly engineers the fall of Anne Boleyn in a tighter, colder second volume of the Tudor trilogy.

like.r: Another history from the inside of a deadly court, narrated with sly irony.
The same court retold as a popular drama, faster and more romantic.
Another Henry VIII-era story about conscience and power, from the other side of the table.

h: Ursula Todd keeps dying and being born again in 1910, trying each time to get it right; a century of England in many versions.

like.r: Another war-shadowed novel that bends time and lingers on death without being solemn.
The comedy of getting repeated tries at a life, here with far lighter stakes.
A gentler, more consoling take on the many-lives idea.

h: In an unnamed Belfast of rumor and threat, a girl who reads while walking draws the attention of a married paramilitary; long, comic, claustrophobic.

like.r: The great Irish stream-of-consciousness novel, more ambitious and more difficult.
Another novel of a community under constant surveillance, set in a fantasy state.

like.t: In the Name of the Father
like.r: A closer-to-the-ground take on the Troubles and what it did to ordinary people.

h: A gentle boy in 1980s Glasgow tries to love and save his alcoholic mother while the world around them hardens.

like.r: A memoir with a similar poor, alcohol-ridden family and a child's resilient eye.
Another devastating story of love that cannot fix the damage.
Another look at working-class Scotland and addiction, loud and darkly comic rather than tender.

h: Twelve mostly Black British women, linked by one theater opening, are told in free-flowing, unpunctuated verse-like prose.

like.r: Another multi-voiced portrait of modern multiracial London, funnier and more traditional in form.
A foundational novel about Black women's friendship and survival.
A more linear novel with similar interests in race, womanhood and migration.

t: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
h: A murdered war photographer wakes in a bureaucratic afterlife with seven moons to reveal where his pictures are hidden; wild, bleak and funny.

like.r: Another satirical, magical-tinged novel about a South Asian nation torn by politics.

like.t: A Brief History of Seven Killings
like.r: Another polyphonic novel of political violence and the dead who still talk.
A far lighter take on a bureaucratic afterlife populated by chattering ghosts.

h: A Dublin mother in a sliding authoritarian Ireland tries to keep her family together; breathless, unbroken paragraphs of mounting dread.

like.r: The classic of a free society hardening around one woman, more focused on gender.
Another bleak, unrelenting story built around a parent's fierce love.
A near-future state sliding into oppression, told as a tense chase.

h: Six astronauts on the space station circle the Earth sixteen times in one day; a hushed, glowing meditation, not a thriller.

like.r: A more unsettling and philosophical story of humans stranded in orbit.
The same breathtaking view of Earth, with panic and survival instead of contemplation.
A slow, spiritual film in orbit that shares the book's hush and fascination with human smallness.

h: A gentle man records his life in an endless house of statues and tides, until signs arrive that someone else is there.

like.r: The source of the infinite-building idea, in a few vertiginous pages.

like.t: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
like.r: Another short, strange, tender story where the mundane borders on myth.
A sunny, innocent man in a world that is not what it seems.

h: A boy escapes a Barbados plantation in a flying machine with an eccentric inventor and wanders the world as a young man.

like.r: Another inventive escape-from-slavery story, more allegorical and bleak.
A boy's adventure on the high seas, which this novel echoes and complicates.
A harrowing, grounded view of the bondage Edugyan's hero flees.

h: A Black farmer in Los Angeles reinstates slavery and segregation in his neighborhood, with a savage and constantly funny narrator.

like.r: The classic comic-tragic odyssey of a Black narrator, with a similar wry surrealism.
The master of absurd satire turned on institutional logic.
A wild satirical comedy about race and capitalism in a surreal modern America.

h: A Vietnamese double agent in California reports to Saigon's enemies while watching Americans make a movie about the war.

like.r: Another novel of Vietnam and divided loyalties, colder and more concise.
The Hollywood Vietnam film the book mocks, a great fever dream in its own right.
The American side of the same war, told in fragments and memory.

h: A kidnapper, prisoner and spy in North Korea moves up and down a regime of lies; a savage, funny, tender epic.

like.r: The founding dystopia of total control, here echoed in a real state.
Nonfiction portraits of ordinary North Koreans, to hold the novel against.
A different surveillance state, treated with great humanity.

h: A mixed-race Mississippi family drives to pick up a father from prison, carrying a ghost with them; rough, lyrical and haunted.

like.r: The model for combining haunting and history, denser and more mythic.
Another Mississippi family journey told in many voices.
Two Mississippi families in different eras, bound by land and prejudice.

h: A 13-year-old Ojibwe boy investigates the assault on his mother when the law's jurisdictional gaps stall everything.

like.r: A coming-of-age through a legal injustice, in a very different community.
Another contemporary Native American novel that mixes sorrow and wry humor.
A violent crime on a reservation and a similar tangle of jurisdiction.

t: A Brief History of Seven Killings
h: A dozen violent, profane voices tell the attempt on a reggae star's life and the decade of Jamaican politics and drugs that followed.

like.r: Another sprawling, many-voiced epic about power and American history.
A shorter, funnier novel with the same jazzy, unbound voice.
A multi-decade, sprawling look at a violent underworld and the music, drugs and corruption around it.

h: Two hired killers ride toward California in the Gold Rush; deadpan, bloody, and surprisingly tender about brotherhood.

like.r: Another dry, funny, first-person western with an eccentric voice.
A far more savage and mythic western of travelling killers.
The film adaptation, a warm, wry take on the same brothers' road.

h: A five-year-old narrates life in the single room that he and his mother share, and what happens when they leave it.

like.r: Another disturbing event told through a child-like voice, with a more spiritual feeling.
The faithful film, with the same intense claustrophobia and tenderness.

like.t: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
like.r: Another novel whose unusual narrator reframes the ordinary world.

h: Three Brown University grads in 1982 tangle over love, depression and literary theory; a campus novel that doubles as a Jane Austen homage.

like.r: The marriage-plot tradition this novel honors and complicates.
Another bookish college novel of intense friendships, with a darker turn.
Another post-grad love triangle about drifting after the humanities.

h: A Minnesota couple who looked perfect fall apart over thirty years of affairs, rivalries and bad political bets; sprawling, sharp and bleakly comic.

like.r: Franzen's earlier, equally big dysfunction-family novel.
A classic of American domestic discontent, narrower and more lyrical.
A suburban family's hypocrisies slowly exposed, played as satire and tragedy.

h: Two London girls bond over dance and diverge over decades, as the narrator shadows a pop star and discovers her own place.

like.r: Smith's exuberant debut, more comic and more crowded.
The classic portrait of a girlhood friendship that becomes a lifelong pull.
Another story of friendship and fame in the music business, though glossier.

h: Chicago in 1985 loses its friends to AIDS, while in 2015 a woman looks for her lost daughter in Paris; devastating and humane.

like.r: Another novel of tightly bound male friendships in grief, though more extreme.
A queer 1980s novel with an urbane, satirical edge and AIDS arriving.
Another look at the AIDS crisis, as a campaign against indifference.

h: A marriage told twice: first the husband's radiant account, then his wife's, which tilts everything you were told.

like.r: Another marriage told through opposing perspectives, with thriller mechanics and a more cynical tone.
A bleaker, older dissection of a marriage's rot.
The classic of one story told from conflicting angles.

h: Cyril, cast out of his Irish village as a boy, lives seven decades in search of love, family and belonging; Dickensian and warmly comic.

like.r: Another gay man's whole life told with great pathos, but without Boyne's comedy.
The classic of Irish hardship rendered with humor.
Another story of Irish church cruelty and a search for family, told gently.

h: A black-and-white circus that appears without warning hosts a duel between two young magicians who fall in love.

like.r: A more elaborate and wry magical rivalry in historical England.
A darker, creepier carnival that arrives in town.
Another rivalry between two magicians, with a harder edge and puzzle plot.

t: The Book of Form and Emptiness
h: After his father's death a boy starts hearing objects speak, and the book itself narrates; odd, warm and full of library love.

like.t: A Tale for the Time Being
like.r: Ozeki's earlier novel, another dual story that mixes Zen, magic and literature.

like.t: The Storied Life of A. J. Fikry
like.r: A simpler, more sentimental novel about books healing lives.
Another story where ordinary objects and spaces come alive to help a child grow.

h: Two sisters in occupied France resist the Nazis in different ways, one by hiding children and the other by guiding pilots to safety.

like.t: All the Light We Cannot See
like.r: A more lyrical, structurally intricate novel about France under occupation.
Another popular, moving Second World War story centered on ordinary courage.
A far starker and more historical account of rescue in the war.

h: A Texas farm wife flees the Dust Bowl for California with her children, and finds hunger and hostility there too.

like.r: The classic of the same migration, broader, angrier and more political.
Hannah's wartime novel, with another courageous woman and equal tearjerker intent.
A quiet modern story of Americans displaced and on the road.

h: On one summer day at a Cape Cod family retreat, a married woman weighs her husband against her oldest love while an old trauma leaks into the story.

like.r: Another long, unfinished love story, cooler and less sensual.
Another family entangled by an old summer decision across decades.
Another sun-drenched summer of longing and a love that stays with you.

h: Three generations of a Kerala family carry a mysterious curse of drowning, as doctors search for its cause; big, humane and patient.

like.r: The author's earlier medical epic, set in Ethiopia and just as devoted to doctors and family.
Another Kerala family story, more lyrical, fragmentary and tragic.
A moving Indian family drama about belonging and roots.

h: Four texts offer different accounts of a Wall Street tycoon and his wife, and the fortune between them; a puzzle about who gets to tell money's story.

like.r: The classic of vast wealth and an elusive, remade self.
Another elegant novel about financial fraud with a haunted, fractured structure.
Many accounts of a magnate, none of them quite whole.

h: A lonely widow who cleans an aquarium befriends a grumpy giant Pacific octopus who knows more than he's saying.

like.r: Another warm, funny story of a grieving loner finding connection.
Another quirky story of loneliness opening up through unexpected company.
The documentary of a human and an octopus whose bond changes him.

h: A 36-year-old woman who loves her job at a Tokyo convenience store is pressured to marry and move on; deadpan, short and unsettling.

like.r: Another detached narrator who doesn't feel what society expects.
Another outsider narrator looking askance at a life she can't escape, darker.
A contented Tokyo worker whose routine has its own quiet dignity.

h: In a small Tokyo cafe you can go back in time, but only until your coffee cools; four gentle stories of regret and what cannot be changed.

like.r: Another short, soft Japanese book where grief is absorbed in small domestic rituals.
Another consoling novel about second chances and what regret teaches.
A Japanese film about death and family handled with great gentleness.

t: Colorless Tsukuru Tazaki and His Years of Pilgrimage
h: Years after his four closest friends cut him off without explanation, a lonely railway engineer travels to find out why; calm, wistful, unresolved.

like.r: Murakami's most realistic and heartbreaking novel, in the same elegiac key.
Another quiet novel of an older man revisiting what happened with youthful friends.
A slow Japanese drama that, like Murakami's story, treats grief and unspoken truths with patience.
